argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only on a caveated basis. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and successful general launch-configuration checks support launch readiness at the system level, but the same record also shows that post-visit instruction summarization is a named deployment context whose evals are queued and not in the packet. The overbroad claim is not that certification is impossible; it is that the current draft can be treated as clean certification. The supportable position is certification with an explicit model-card limitation or unresolved-gap disclosure for that named context.
claims_about_business_cost: No admissible evidence establishes a business-cost basis for overriding the disclosure requirement. The risk-weighted governance point is narrower: escalation is unnecessary if the auditor records that certification is supportable only with the required limitation disclosure, because that treatment aligns the packet with the evidence already in the record.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not require denying certification whenever a named-context eval gap exists; it requires disclosing material limitations or evaluation gaps for named launch use cases unless they are resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On the current admissible record, general checks cannot be read as coverage for post-visit instruction summarization, and the draft statement of no known telehealth discharge-planning limitations is not supportable. The compliant path is to treat that area as unknown or limited in the certification materials.
concessions: The current packet does not support clean certification with no deployment limitation.
There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure correction has already been completed.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or completed evals for post-visit instruction summarization.
